title.narrative: Provision of Specialized Protection Services for Drought-Affected Women, Girls, and Children in Bossaso, Puntland

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to enhance access to lifesaving, survivor-centred, and child-focused protection services for drought-affected women, girls, boys, and caregivers in Bossaso, Bari Region, through integrated Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Child Protection (CP) interventions. Prolonged drought across Puntland has displaced thousands of families into peri-urban and rural settlements, heightening exposure to sexual violence, intimate partner violence (IPV), family separation, early marriage, neglect, and exploitation. The project responds directly to the 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) and the Somalia SHF Reserve Allocation Strategy – Drought in the North (2025), both prioritising protection for populations in high-risk drought-affected areas.ltbrgtAMARD will provide specialised, survivor-centred case management for children at risk, unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), and survivors of GBV, including IPV and sexual violence. Activities will include Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR), alternative care arrangements, Psychological First Aid (PFA), and structured psychosocial support (PSS) delivered by trained case workers through fixed and mobile teams. GBV services will focus on confidential case management, dissemination of updated referral pathways, and training and mentoring of 20 midwives, nurses, and allied responders on Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) and IPV treatment in accordance with national protocols.ltbrgtTo reduce financial barriers that limit survivor access to care, AMARD will integrate sector-specific unconditional cash assistance into GBV case management, following the Somalia Inter-Agency Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) Guidelines (2025) and UNFPA/GBV AoR Cash in GBV Case Management SOPs (2025). Each eligible survivor will receive a one-off grant of USD 40 to cover urgent protection-related needs such as transport to health facilities, temporary shelter, medical or legal fees, or dignity items. Dignity and survivor-support kits will also be distributed to promote hygiene, safety, and dignity for women and girls.ltbrgtComplementary community mobilisation and awareness sessions will reach approximately 3,000 people, tackling stigma, harmful norms, and misinformation on GBV and CP, while increasing understanding of available referral pathways and reporting channels. Messaging will integrate Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) principles. AMARD’s toll-free hotline (2245) will remain accessible for confidential feedback, complaints, and referrals.ltbrgtThe project will directly assist about 9,000 individuals—including 5,200 children and caregivers through CP services and 3,800 women and girls through GBV activities—and indirectly benefit roughly 9,000 additional community members through improved awareness, service coordination, and strengthened local capacities. Implementation will be closely coordinated with the Protection Cluster, GBV and CP Areas of Responsibility (AoRs), and local authorities under the Bossaso Area-Based Coordination (ABC) framework to ensure complementarity with ongoing humanitarian actions.ltbrgtOver a six-month period (December 2025 – May 2026), the project will strengthen safety, dignity, and psychosocial resilience among drought-affected populations, while reinforcing community-based prevention, referral, and accountability mechanisms that uphold the Centrality of Protection, AAP, PSEA, and Data Protection and Information-Sharing Protocol (2025) standards.lt/pgt
